record.original_question: For the incompressible Euler equations, is the Cauchy problem ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{infty,q} for 1<q<infty, the range between B^1_{infty,1} and the Zygmund space B^1_{infty,infty}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d\ge 2$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,\qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,$$
where $u:[0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is the velocity field and $p$ is the pressure. For $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, the inhomogeneous Besov space $B^s_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ consists of tempered distributions $f$ for which
$$\|f\|_{B^s_{\infty,q}} := \Big(\sum_{j\ge -1} 2^{jsq}\|\Delta_j f\|_{L^\infty}^q\Big)^{1/q} < \infty,$$
where $(\Delta_j)_{j\ge -1}$ is a Littlewood–Paley dyadic decomposition (with the usual modification for $q=\infty$). It is known that the Euler Cauchy problem is locally well-posed (in the sense of Hadamard) in $B^1_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and is ill-posed in the Zygmund space $B^1_{\infty,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Question: For every $q$ with $1<q<\infty$, is the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations ill-posed in $B^1_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^d)$?
artifact.category_tag: Euler equations well-posedness in Besov spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Well-posedness in $B^1_{\infty,1}$ (Pak–Park; Guo–Li–Yin) and ill-posedness/discontinuous dependence in $B^s_{p,\infty}$ (including $B^1_{\infty,\infty}$) are known. Recent work has extended ill-posedness in $B^s_{p,\infty}$ spaces, but a definitive answer for the intermediate range $B^1_{\infty,q}$ with $1<q<\infty$ does not appear in the searched literature, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Ill-posedness in B^s_{p,infty} of the Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Solution map is not continuous in the Besov spaces B^s_{p,infty} for s>1+d/p, 1<=p<=infty.
status_evidence.claim: Ill-posedness has been established in the third-index $\infty$ case but not directly for $1<q<\infty$.

status_evidence.title: Local well-posedness of the incompressible Euler equations in B^1_{infty,1}
status_evidence.snippet: Local well-posedness of Euler in B^1_{infty,1}.

status_evidence.title: Strong ill-posedness of the incompressible Euler equation in borderline Sobolev spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Bourgain–Li strong ill-posedness in borderline Sobolev/Besov spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The endpoint $q=\infty$ (Zygmund) and related borderline cases are ill-posed.
